analysis.title: US Midterms: Historical Equity-Volume Patterns and the Balance of Power
key_insights: UBS S&T reviewed equity volumes around the 2014, 2018 and 2022 midterms across the S&P and several European indices. Midterms have not materially moved equity volumes in the US or developed Europe.
The most consistent pattern is a short-lived volume lull around Election Day and T+1, concentrated in US and developed European markets.
The S&P traded below its previous 20-day average volume on midterm Election Day in all three samples: -15% in 2014, -22% in 2018, -6% in 2022.
Beyond T+1 there is no consistent pattern. Volumes stayed subdued after 2018, briefly recovered after 2014, and rose sharply from T+2 in 2022.
In 2022 all eight indices examined moved above their 20-day averages at T+2. UBS cautions against attributing this to the midterm result without separating it from other market drivers at the time.
UBS concludes the midterms themselves have generally not driven volumes and the broader market backdrop has mattered more.

For 2026 the relevant question is whether the result produces a policy outcome large enough to break the historical pattern. Channels named: fiscal policy, shutdown and debt-ceiling risk, Senate confirmations, and the future composition of the Fed.

Split control (for example a Democratic House) raises the potential for gridlock, fiscal brinkmanship and shutdown or debt-ceiling risk. A blue sweep would increase congressional influence over Senate confirmations and oversight.
Even under divided government the administration would keep substantial authority over tariffs, trade investigations, energy and banking regulation, drug pricing and foreign investment.
Execution takeaway: allow for softer liquidity immediately around the vote, but do not position for a mechanical post-election volume rebound.

sector_views.sector: Autos, construction, consumer, financials, energy, tariff-sensitive names
sector_views.rationale: UBS lists these as names to watch in a red sweep, given the focus on tariffs, deregulation, energy and fiscal policy. No directional call.

sector_views.sector: Healthcare, technology/AI, semiconductors, financials/payments, housing, clean energy
sector_views.rationale: UBS lists these as names to watch in a blue sweep, given the focus on oversight, healthcare, housing, clean energy and technology regulation. No directional call.

trade_ideas.description: Split control scenario: extra focus on the European lines in the GOP Midterms Risk basket (UBXXMID), which tracks stocks expected to underperform if Republicans lose the House or Senate
trade_ideas.rationale: A Democratic House raises the potential for gridlock and fiscal, shutdown and debt-ceiling risk.

trade_ideas.description: Blue sweep scenario: extra focus on the GOP Midterms Risk basket (UBXXMID) and watch healthcare, technology/AI, semiconductors, financials/payments, housing and clean energy
trade_ideas.rationale: Democratic control of both chambers would increase influence over Senate confirmations, Fed appointments and oversight of the administration.

trade_ideas.description: All outcomes: watch stocks in the US Exposure thematic basket (UBXEUSA)
trade_ideas.rationale: UBS lists it as the basket to watch regardless of the election result.

risk_factors: The 2026 result produces a meaningful policy or macro catalyst, which would make the historical midterm volume pattern less informative.
Split control raises shutdown and debt-ceiling risk and makes major partisan legislation less likely.
Prolonged uncertainty over control of Congress.
Senate control could affect the future composition and reaction function of the FOMC.
vol_and_positioning: S&P volume on midterm Election Day versus its prior 20-day average: -15% in 2014, -22% in 2018, -6% in 2022.
Thinner activity around Election Day and T+1 is the repeatable feature, particularly in US and developed European markets. No consistent volume pattern after T+1.
In 2022 all eight indices examined rose above their 20-day average volume at T+2.
UBS suggests allowing for softer liquidity immediately around the vote rather than positioning for a post-election volume rebound.

theme_stances.evidence: midterms have not materially moved the needle on equity volumes
